name: French Open
stakes: This week offered PV Sindhu a significant Super 750 final appearance, while other Indian shuttlers sought crucial ranking points and momentum ahead of the season's final stretch.
summary:
India's campaign at the French Open Super 750 event concluded with a mixed bag of results, highlighted by PV Sindhu's impressive run to the women's singles final. Sindhu, ranked 11th, displayed remarkable grit throughout the tournament, ultimately falling to her formidable rival, An Se-young, in a hard-fought championship match. This runner-up finish marks her best-ever performance at the French Open, a significant boost as the season progresses.

However, other Indian hopefuls faced early exits. The top men's doubles pair, Satwik & Chirag, ranked 6th, were unable to advance past the Round of 32, a surprising early departure for the usually consistent duo. Young talent Unnati Hooda, ranked 18th in women's singles, also saw her journey end in the opening round. Similarly, the promising women's doubles pair of Treesa & Gayatri, ranked 19th, bowed out in the Round of 32. Attention now shifts to the upcoming Hylo Open, where Sindhu and Lakshya Sen are set to lead the Indian challenge.
